text:
If a rocket runs on a fuel $(C_{15}H_{30})$ and liquid oxygen, the weight of oxygen required and $CO_{2}$ released for every litre of fuel respectively are :

(Given : density of the fuel is 0.756 g/mL)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$C_{15}H_{30} +$ $\frac{45}{2}O_{2}$ $\to$ $15CO_{2} + 15H_{2}O$

Given, volume of fuel = 1L = 1000 ml

And density of fuel = 0.756 g/ml

We know,

$d=\frac{w}{v}$

$\Rightarrow 0.756=\frac{w}{1000}$

$\Rightarrow$ w = 756 gm

$\therefore$ weight of fuel = 756 gm

Molar mass of $C_{15}H_{30} = 15$ $\times$ 12 + 30 = 210

$\therefore$ Moles of $C_{15}H_{30} =$ $\frac{756}{210}$

From equation you can see,

1 mole of $C_{15}H_{30}$ react with $\frac{45}{2}$ mole of $O_{2}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{756}{210}$ moles of $C_{15}H_{30}$ react with $\frac{45}{2}\times \frac{756}{210}$ moles of $O_{2}$

$\therefore$ Moles of $O_{2}$ required = $\frac{45}{2}\times \frac{756}{210}$

$\therefore$ Mass of $O_{2}$ required = $\frac{45}{2}\times \frac{756}{210}$ $\times$ 32 = 2592 g

Also,

From 1 mole of $C_{15}H_{30} 15$ moles of $CO_{2}$ formed

$\therefore$ From $\frac{756}{210}$ moles of $C_{15}H_{30} 15$ $\times$ $\frac{756}{210}$ moles of $CO_{2}$ formed

$\therefore$ Moles of $CO_{2}$ formed = 15 $\times$ $\frac{756}{210}$

$\therefore$ Mass of $CO_{2}$ formed = 15 $\times$ $\frac{756}{210}$ $\times$ 44 = 2376 g
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

      (b) n = 3, $l$ $= 2, m_{l} = 1, m_{s} = +$ $\frac{1}{2}$

      (b) n = 3, $l$ $= 2, m_{l} =$ $-1, m_{s} =$ $-\frac{1}{2}$

solution.body:
For degenerate orbitals, only the value of m must

same.

text:
Match List - I with List - II :

  
    
    List - I
    
    List -II
  

  
    (A)
    $[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}$
    (I)
    $sp^{3}d$
  
  
    (B)
    $BrF_{5}$
    (II)
    $d^{2}sp^{3}$
  
  
    (C)
    $PCl_{5}$
    (III)
    $dsp^{2}$
  
  
    (D)
    $[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}$
    (IV)
    $sp^{3}d^{2}$
  

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{PtCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Pt}{}^{2+}$ is $5d^{8}$; as a 5d ion it pairs the eight electrons into four 5d orbitals and uses the empty 5d, 6s and two 6p orbitals, so it is $dsp^{2}$ (square planar) (III).

$\mathrm{BrF}{}_{5}$: Br has 7 valence electrons; 5 form Br–F bonds and 2 remain as one lone pair, so there are 6 electron pairs and the hybridisation is $sp^{3}d^{2}$ (square pyramidal) (IV).

$\mathrm{PCl}{}_{5}$: P has 5 bond pairs and no lone pair, so it is $sp^{3}d$ (trigonal bipyramidal) (I).

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$; strong-field $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ pairs these into three 3d orbitals, leaving two inner 3d orbitals for $d^{2}sp^{3}$ (II).

The matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

For a reaction at equilibrium

A(g) $⇌$ B(g) + $\frac{1}{2}$ C(g)

the relation between dissociation constant (K), degree of dissociation ($α$) and equilibrium pressure (p) is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Now,

$K_{P}$ or $K=\frac{P_{B}\times (P_{C})^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}{P_{A}}$

$=\frac{\left (\frac{α}{1+\dfrac{α}{2}}\right )P\times \left [\left (\frac{\dfrac{α}{2}}{1+\dfrac{α}{2}}\right )P\right ]^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}{\left (\frac{1-α}{1+\dfrac{α}{2}}\right )P}$

$=\frac{\left (\frac{2α}{2+α}\right )P\times \left [\left (\frac{α}{2+α}\right )P\right ]^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}{\left (\frac{2(1-α)}{2+α}\right )P}$

$=\frac{α^{\dfrac{3}{2}}.P^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}{(1-α)(2+α)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}$

text:
Two statements are given below :

Statement I : The melting point of monocarboxylic acid with even number of carbon atoms is higher than that of with odd number of carbon atoms acid immediately below and above it in the series.

Statement II : The solubility of monocarboxylic acids in water decreases with increase in molar mass.

Choose the most appropriate option :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement (I) is correct as monocarboxylic acids
with even number of carbon atoms show better
packing efficiency in the solid state, statement (II) is
also correct as the solubility of carboxylic acids
decreases with an increase in molar mass due to
increase in the hydrophobic portion with an increase in
the number of carbon atoms.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text:
$2O_{3}(g)$ $⇌$ $3O_{2}(g)$

At 300 K, ozone is fifty percent dissociated. The standard free energy change at this temperature and 1 atm pressure is ($-) ____________ J$ mol$^{-1}. ($Nearest integer)

[Given : ln 1.35 = 0.3 and $R = 8.3 J K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2\mathrm{O}_{3}(\mathrm{g})_{1-x}⇌3\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})_{\frac{3\mathrm{x}}{2}}$

Given, $x=0.5$

$\therefore \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{[3(0.5)]^{3}\times 1}{[2]^{3}\times (0.5)^{2}\times 1.25}$

$\therefore \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{27}{8}\times \frac{0.5}{1.25}=1.35$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ } & =-2.303\mathrm{RT}\log \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{p}} \\  \\ \qquad =-2.303\times 8.3\times 300\log 1.35 \\  \\ \qquad =-8.3\times 300\ln (1.35) \\  \\ \qquad =-747\mathrm{J}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text: In the cobalt-carbonyl complex : [$Co_{2}(CO)_{8}$], number of Co-Co bonds is "X" and terminal CO ligands is "Y". $X + Y = ___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In its solid-state structure, $[\mathrm{Co}{}_{2}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{8}]$ has the two Co atoms joined by one Co–Co bond and also bridged by two CO groups.

Each Co carries three terminal CO groups, so the number of terminal CO is $2\times 3=6$; with the 2 bridging CO this accounts for all 8 CO.

$X=1$ and $Y=6$, so $X+Y=1+6=7$.

Hence, the answer is 7.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift

text:
Number of electrophilic centres in the given compound is $_______________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An electrophilic centre is an electron-deficient atom that can accept an electron pair from a nucleophile.

The carbonyl carbon is electrophilic because of the polar $\mathrm{C}^{δ+}=\mathrm{O}^{δ-}$ bond.

The C=C is conjugated with the C=O, so resonance places a positive charge on the $β$-carbon (the alkene carbon farther from C=O); it is attacked by nucleophiles in conjugate (1,4) addition.

$\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}⟷\mathrm{C}^{+}-\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}^{-}$

The nitrile carbon is electrophilic because of the polar $\mathrm{C}^{δ+}\equiv \mathrm{N}^{δ-}$ bond.


[IMG]

The aromatic ring carbons, the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ groups and the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ carbon carry no such positive polarisation, so the compound has 3 electrophilic centres.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Morning Shift
